title: The Passage of Patagonia's dry side
premise: Salvage diver Odile Amberdale is hired to strip a wrecked navy freighter off Patagonia's arid eastern coast, where the crew finds a sealed strongbox containing a prospector's map to a river source the government has erased from every chart. The dying prospector, Tomás Quillén, trades her the map for a promise: carry it upstream and tell the truth about what was buried there in 1974. Pursued by navy contractors who sank the freighter themselves, Odile and her loyal but conflicted deckhand Mateo follow the shrinking river into canyon country as the dry season closes the waterways. At the source they uncover a drowned settlement and the navy's original crime — and Odile must choose between selling her silence for survival or broadcasting the truth, ending with her broadcasting it and paying the price of exile from the sea she loves.
about_author: Juniper Pemberton is a former marine surveyor who spent six years charting remote waterways in southern South America before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about landscapes that keep secrets and the people stubborn enough to dig them up.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Working the wreck of the freighter Vencedora off the arid coast, she measures her life in nautical miles since leaving home ten years ago. When her team raises a sealed strongbox the navy's liaison orders destroyed, she hides it instead. Emotional beat: restless competence masking an old wound.

chapters.title: The Prospector's Bargain
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In a dusty port cantina she tracks down Tomás Quillén, the map's author, now dying of lung disease. He trades her the full map for a sworn promise to follow the river to its source and speak what happened there. That night, navy contractors burn her dive boat. Beat: a promise made under pressure.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Mateo's POV. The deckhand, torn between loyalty to Odile and fear of the men hunting them, pilots them inland in a shallow-draft skiff as the river narrows. First tailing vehicle spotted; first lie told to a checkpoint officer. Beat: loyalty tested at the first fork in the river.

chapters.title: The Town That Isn't on Charts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They reach Río Seco, a settlement absent from every map, where old residents recognize Quillén's name and go silent when soldiers visit. An elderly woman slips Odile a photograph of the town before 1974. Beat: the past has teeth, and the town remembers.

chapters.title: Dry Season Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Mateo's POV. The river drops measurably each day; Odile calculates they have eleven days before the upper gorge becomes impassable. A contractor patrol forces them to abandon the skiff and portage on foot through thorn country. Beat: the price of survival begins coming due.

chapters.title: What Mateo Knew
chapters.summary: Mateo's POV. Confronted by Odile after he's caught radioing his brother in the port, Mateo confesses he was approached weeks ago to report on her dives — and refused until fear won. Trust fractures; they travel a day without speaking. Beat: betrayal confessed, loyalty renegotiated.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Echoes
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the narrowing canyon they find the wreck of a 1970s convoy truck and human remains with navy-issue tags. Contractors ambush them at dusk; a guide from Río Seco dies covering their escape. Beat: grief hardens into resolve.

chapters.title: The Drowned Village
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They reach the source: a reservoir behind an unlisted dam, its flooded village visible in clear water — the site Quillén dove as a young man. Odile free-dives the church bell tower and recovers the documentary evidence Quillén hid there. Beat: awe and horror entwined.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Cornered at the dam by the contractor commander, Odile is offered money, silence, and safe passage — everything she has measured her life in miles to avoid needing. Mateo steps between them, choosing her side at last. Beat: the climax of choice over survival.

chapters.title: Where the River Begins
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They escape down the spillway as the dry season ends and the first rains come, transmitting the evidence from a mountain relay station. Odile loses her salvage license and access to the sea, but gains the truth and an unexpected home in Río Seco. Beat: exile accepted, inheritance claimed.
